justifications.c1: Many independent regulator-sourced fines well above £5k: £100k chemical manufacturer (HSE, search-confirmed), £600k Places for People (search-confirmed), ~£204k car dealer, £140k Stonewater, £40k NHS trust, plus civil awards £8.5k–£60k and six figures; but losses follow years of exposure, so 12-month payback per site is not shown.
justifications.c2: Vibrating tools are used daily and trigger-time estimation is a routine task (hire-firm HAV guides, HSE points system), but no mandated daily or weekly record frequency is sourced, and new HAVS cases are rare per employer (~220/yr GB IIDB).
justifications.c3: Paid workarounds are priced: HAVi/Pulsar tool timers £91–£100, Castle HAV kit £3,769, Reactec's £1m Network Rail contract, plus paper points systems and hire-firm calculators; evidence (Safe Work Australia, Canadian Acoustics) shows self-estimates are unreliable, though labour time is not quantified.
justifications.c4: Control of Vibration at Work Regulations 2005 set statutory ELV/EAV with risk-assessment and health-surveillance duties, and HSE enforces regularly (prosecutions 2019–2026, search-confirmed); monitoring itself is not mandated, so not a full 10.
justifications.c5: Prosecuted employers span housing, NHS, chemicals and motor trade, and Network Rail bought at scale, but no job advert or role description shows an H&S manager holding a HAV-monitoring budget (recorded not found).
justifications.c6: Major UK hire firms (Speedy, Brandon, GAP, HSS, A-Plant) already supply Reactec HAVmeters (search-confirmed, c.2010–2012 Reactec PR) and GAP currently catalogues EAVE ToolWarden tags, so the hire channel already bundles comparable monitoring.
justifications.c7: Crowded and partly commoditised: Reactec HAVwear/R-Link, Castle HAVi, Pulsar HAVi+ (£98, 'no subscriptions'), EAVE ToolWarden, HAV-Sentry, HAVSPRO; hire-fleet tool tags have existed since 2008–09, leaving only a narrow per-hire on-tool-vibration gap.
justifications.c8: Cheap pre-certified BLE modules ($4.71–$8.37) and coin-cell battery benchmarks are evidenced, but measurement validity (HSE Buxton testing, palm vs wrist), harsh tool-mounted conditions, ATEX variants for some sites and reliance on phone/gateway connectivity add risk.
justifications.c9: Ongoing risk-assessment and health-surveillance duties give data lasting value, but no retention schedule for exposure records is sourced, Pulsar explicitly sells without subscriptions and no competitor subscription price was found.
justifications.c10: Regulator data (HSE IIDB statistics and press releases), trade press (Construction Management, PBC Today, Fleet News, Local Government Lawyer), first-hand practitioner forums (IOSH, ArbTalk) and law-firm claim cases.

weakest: The hire-fleet tool-tag concept already exists (Reactec HAVmeters in Speedy, Brandon, GAP and HSS fleets; EAVE ToolWarden at GAP) and cheap £91–£100 timers with no subscription cap pricing.
